arxiv-1410-5077.title: On the Provenance of Linked Data Statistics
arxiv-1410-5077.creator: William Waites
arxiv-1410-5077.description: Abstract As the amount of linked data published on the web grows, attempts are being made to describe and measure it. However even basic statistics about a graph, such as its size, are difficult to express in a uniform and predictable way.

arxiv-2011-09930.title: Cosmological horizons radiate
arxiv-2011-09930.creator: Ulf Leonhardt
arxiv-2011-09930.description: Abstract Gibbons and Hawking [Phys. Rev. D 15 , 2738 (1977)] have shown that the horizon of de Sitter space emits radiation in the same way as the event horizon of the black hole. But actual cosmological horizons are not event horizons, except in de Sitter space.

arxiv-2105-12433.title: Estimating the Uncertainty of Neural Network Forecasts for Influenza Prevalence Using Web Search Activity
arxiv-2105-12433.creator: Michael Morris, Peter Hayes, Ingemar J. Cox, Vasileios Lampos
arxiv-2105-12433.description: Abstract Influenza is an infectious disease with the potential to become a pandemic, and hence, forecasting its prevalence is an important undertaking for planning an effective response. Research has found that web search activity can be used to improve influenza models.

arxiv-2110-10150.title: Summ N : A Multi-Stage Summarization Framework for Long Input Dialogues and Documents
arxiv-2110-10150.creator: Yusen Zhang, Ansong Ni, Ziming Mao, Chen Henry Wu, Chenguang Zhu Budhaditya Deb Ahmed H. Awadallah, Dragomir Radev Rui Zhang
arxiv-2110-10150.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yusen Zhang, Ansong Ni, Ziming Mao, Chen Henry Wu, Chenguang Zhu Budhaditya Deb Ahmed H. Awadallah, Dragomir Radev Rui Zhang. Text summarization helps readers capture salient information from documents, news, interviews, and meetings. However, most state-of-the-art pretrained language models (LM) are unable to efficiently process long text for many summarization tasks. In this paper, we propose Summ N , a simple, flexible, and effective multi-stage framework for input texts that are longer than the maximum context length of typical pretrained LMs.

arxiv-2110-11658.title: Accelerating NBODY6 with a GPU-Enabled Particle-Particle Particle-Tree Scheme 2021 Accelerating NBODY6 with a GPU-Enabled Particle-Particle Particle-Tree Scheme – 3
arxiv-2110-11658.creator: Anthony D. Arnold, Holger Baumgardt, Long Wang
arxiv-2110-11658.description: Abstract We describe a modified version of the nbody6 code for simulating star clusters which greatly improves computational efficiency while sacrificing little in the way of accuracy. The distant force calculator is replaced by a GPU-enabled Barnes-Hut code, and integration is done with a standard leap frog scheme.

arxiv-2209-13547.title: Interactivism in Spoken Dialogue Systems
arxiv-2209-13547.creator: Teresa Rodríguez Muñoz, Emily Ip, Guanyu Huang, Roger K. Moore
arxiv-2209-13547.description: Abstract The interactivism model introduces a dynamic approach to language, communication and cognition. In this work, we explore this fundamental theory in the context of dialogue modelling for spoken dialogue systems (SDS). To extend such a theoretical framework, we present a set of design principles which adhere to central psycholinguistic and communication theories to achieve interactivism in SDS.

arxiv-2211-15050.title: Join-the-Shortest Queue with Abandonment: Critically Loaded and Heavily Overloaded Regimes DOI: XXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: POMACS Volume: 37 10
arxiv-2211-15050.creator: Prakirt R. Jhunjhunwala, Martin Zubeldia, Siva Theja Maguluri
arxiv-2211-15050.description: Abstract . We consider a load balancing system comprised of a fixed number of single server queues, operating under the well-known Join-the-Shortest Queue policy, and where jobs/customers are impatient and abandon if they do not receive service after some (random) amount of time.

arxiv-2302-05487.title: Cryogenic nano-imaging of second-order moiré superlattices
arxiv-2302-05487.creator: Niels C.H. Hesp, Sergi Batlle-Porro, Roshan Krishna Kumar, Hitesh Agarwal, David Barcons-Ruiz, Hanan Herzig Sheinfux, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Petr Stepanov, Frank H.L. Koppens
arxiv-2302-05487.description: Abstract Second-order superlattices form when moiré superlattices of similar dimensions interfere with each other, leading to even larger superlattice periodicities. These crystalline structures have been engineered utilizing two-dimensional (2D) materials such as graphene and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) under specific alignment conditions.

arxiv-2303-14624.creator: Jiacheng Wang, Hongyang Du, Dusit Niyato, Zehui Xiong, Jiawen Kang
arxiv-2303-14624.description: Abstract Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), coupled with a surge in training data, have led to the widespread use of AI for digital content generation, with ChatGPT serving as an representative example. Despite the increased efficiency and diversity, the inherent instability of AI models poses a persistent challenge in guiding these models to produce the desired content for users.

arxiv-2304-06163.title: Cosymplectic groupoids Thanks: RLF was partially supported by NSF grant DMS-2003223.
arxiv-2304-06163.creator: Rui Loja Fernandes, David Iglesias Ponte
arxiv-2304-06163.description: Abstract . A cosymplectic groupoid is a Lie groupoid with a multiplicative cosymplectic structure. We provide several structural results for cosymplectic groupoids and we discuss the relationship between cosymplectic groupoids, Poisson groupoids of corank 1, and oversymplectic groupoids of corank 1. 1. Introduction A cosymplectic groupoid is a Lie groupoid \mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M equipped with a multiplicative cosymplectic structure (\omega,\alpha) .

arxiv-2309-13586.title: Task-Oriented Dexterous Hand Pose Synthesis Using Differentiable Grasp Wrench Boundary Estimator
arxiv-2309-13586.creator: Jiayi Chen, Yuxing Chen, Jialiang Zhang, He Wang
arxiv-2309-13586.description: Abstract This work tackles the problem of task-oriented dexterous hand pose synthesis, which involves generating a static hand pose capable of applying a task-specific set of wrenches to manipulate objects. Unlike previous approaches that focus solely on force-closure grasps, which are unsuitable for non-prehensile manipulation tasks ( e.g.

arxiv-2311-06239.title: Argumentation Element Annotation Modeling using XLNet
arxiv-2311-06239.creator: Christopher Ormerod, Amy Burkhardt, Mackenzie Young, and Sue Lottridge
arxiv-2311-06239.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christopher Ormerod, Amy Burkhardt, Mackenzie Young, and Sue Lottridge. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of XLNet, a transformer-based language model, for annotating argumentative elements in persuasive essays. XLNet’s architecture incorporates a recurrent mechanism that allows it to model long-term dependencies in lengthy texts. Fine-tuned XLNet models were applied to three datasets annotated with different schemes - a proprietary dataset using the Annotations for Revisions and Reflections on Writing (ARROW) scheme, the PERSUADE corpus, and the Argument Annotated Essays (AAE) dataset.

arxiv-2402-09549.title: Pareto-Optimal Algorithms for Learning in Games
arxiv-2402-09549.creator: Eshwar Ram Arunachaleswaran, Natalie Collina, Jon Schneider
arxiv-2402-09549.description: Abstract We study the problem of characterizing optimal learning algorithms for playing repeated games against an adversary with unknown payoffs. In this problem, the first player (called the learner) commits to a learning algorithm against a second player (called the optimizer), and the optimizer best-responds by choosing the optimal dynamic strategy for their (unknown but well-defined) payoff.

arxiv-2412-05021.title: Improving data sharing and knowledge transfer via the Neuroelectrophysiology Analysis Ontology (NEAO)
arxiv-2412-05021.creator: Cristiano A. Köhler, Sonja Grün, Michael Denker
arxiv-2412-05021.description: Abstract Describing the processes involved in analyzing data from electrophysiology experiments to investigate the function of neural systems is inherently challenging. On the one hand, data can be analyzed by distinct methods that serve a similar purpose, such as different algorithms to estimate the spectral power content of a measured time series.

arxiv-2501-03066.title: Shock and SEP Modeling Study for the 5 September 2022 SEP Event
arxiv-2501-03066.creator: A. Kouloumvakos, N. Wijsen, I. C. Jebaraj, A. Afanasiev, D. Lario, C. M. S. Cohen, P. Riley, D. G. Mitchell, Z. Ding, A. Vourlidas, J. Giacalone, X. Chen, M. E. Hill

arxiv-2503-20845.title: Unraveling the electronic, vibrational, thermodynamic, optical and piezoelectric properties of LiNbO 3 , LiTaO 3 and Li 2 NbTaO 6 from first-principles calculations
arxiv-2503-20845.creator: Debidutta Pradhan, Rojalin Swain, Souvagya Kumar Biswal and Jagadish Kumar
arxiv-2503-20845.description: Abstract We have investigated the electronic, vibrational, optical, thermal and piezoelectric properties of LiNbO 3 , LiTaO 3 and Li 2 NbTaO 6 using the first-principles calculation based on the density functional theory. It also shows structural phase transition below T c T_{c} due to ionic displacement that may alter the properties of material.

arxiv-2504-17013.title: A Weighted-likelihood framework for class imbalance in Bayesian prediction models
arxiv-2504-17013.creator: Stanley E. Lazic
arxiv-2504-17013.description: Abstract Class imbalance occurs when data used for training classification models has a different number of observations or samples within each category or class. Models built on such data can be biased towards the majority class and have poor predictive performance and generalisation for the minority class.

arxiv-2507-10613.title: Sub-Scaling Laws: On the Role of Data Density and Training Strategies in LLMs
arxiv-2507-10613.creator: Zhengyu Chen, Siqi Wang, Teng Xiao, Yudong Wang, Shiqi Chen, Xunliang Cai, Junxian He, Jingang Wang
arxiv-2507-10613.description: Abstract Traditional scaling laws in natural language processing suggest that increasing model size and training data enhances performance. However, recent studies reveal deviations, particularly in large language models, where performance improvements decelerate—a phenomenon known as sub-scaling. This paper revisits these scaling laws by examining the impact of data quality and training strategies on model performance.

The nuclear 18S rRNA and mitochondrial cox1 of Sarcocystis sp.1 from mangrove snakes (Boiga dendrophila) in Thailand and Sarcocystis sp.2 from a ricefield rat (Rattus argentiventer) in Sumatra were partially sequenced. pmc-10689945.title: Antibacterial and phytochemical analysis of traditional medicinal plants: An alternative therapeutic Approach to conventional antibiotics
pmc-10689945.creator: Asaye Asfaw, Ermias Lulekal, Tamrat Bekele, Asfaw Debella, Asfaw Meresa, Bihonegn Sisay, Sileshi Degu, Abiy Abebe
pmc-10689945.description: The purpose of this study was to carry out antibacterial and phytochemical analyses on six selected medicinal plants that have been traditionally used by the local people to treat and control different diseases. The antibacterial activities of methanolic extracts of these plants were assessed using the Agar well diffusion and Microtiter broth dilution methods.

pmc-11437129.title: Novel 3-dimensional effective regurgitation orifice area quantification serves as a reliable tool to identify severe mitral valve regurgitation
pmc-11437129.creator: Tobias Harm, Frederic-Joaquim Schwarz, Monika Zdanyte, Andreas Goldschmied, Livia Baas, Parwez Aidery, Serhii Shcherbyna, Ioannis Toskas, Timea Keller, Isabela Kast, Juergen Schreieck, Tobias Geisler, Meinrad Paul Gawaz, Karin Anne Lydia Mueller
pmc-11437129.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A precise quantification of mitral regurgitation (MR) severity is essential for treatment and outcome of patients with MR. 3D echocardiography facilitates estimation of MR but selection of patients with necessity of invasive treatment remains challenging. We investigate effective regurgitation orifice area (EROA) quantification by 3D compared to 2D echocardiography in patients with MR and highlight the improved discrimination of MR severity.

pmc-11467340.title: Multi-scale input layers and dense decoder aggregation network for COVID-19 lesion segmentation from CT scans
pmc-11467340.creator: Xiaoke Lan, Wenbing Jin
pmc-11467340.description: Accurate segmentation of COVID-19 lesions from medical images is essential for achieving precise diagnosis and developing effective treatment strategies. Unfortunately, this task presents significant challenges, owing to the complex and diverse characteristics of opaque areas, subtle differences between infected and healthy tissue, and the presence of noise in CT images.

pmc-11478069.title: Thermo- and Photoresponsive Smart Nanomaterial Based on Poly(diethyl vinyl phosphonate)-Capped Gold Nanoparticles
pmc-11478069.creator: Antonio Buonerba, Rosita Lapenta, Francesco Della Monica, Roberto Piacentini, Lucia Baldino, Maria Rosa Scognamiglio, Vito Speranza, Stefano Milione, Carmine Capacchione, Bernhard Rieger, Alfonso Grassi
pmc-11478069.description: A new nanodevice based on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) capped with poly(diethylvinylphosphonate) (PDEVP) has been synthesized, showing interesting photophysical and thermoresponsive properties. The synthesis involves a properly designed Yttriocene catalyst coordinating the vinyl-lutidine (VL) initiator active in diethyl vinyl phosphonate polymerization. The unsaturated PDEVP chain ending was thioacetylated, deacetylated, and reacted with tetrachloroauric acid and sodium borohydride to form PDEVP-VL-capped AuNPs.

pmc-12655098.title: Structural and Functional Insights into Viral and Fungal Proteins Involved in Chronic Inflammation and Their Biologic Treatments
pmc-12655098.creator: Mohamed Halawa, Alicia L. Gallo, Valerie J. Carabetta
pmc-12655098.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chronic inflammation constitutes a significant characteristic of sustained infections caused by viral and fungal pathogens, with a strong correlation to the development of cancer, autoimmune disorders, and tissue fibrosis. Viral proteins such as HIV-1 Tat, HBV X (HBx), HPV E6/E7, and EBV LMP1 modulate the host’s immune signaling pathways, primarily through the activation of the NF-κB signaling cascade and the disruption of cytokine equilibrium.

pmc-13056760.title: Rethinking Obesity Prevention: A Call for Strategic and Operational Clarity
pmc-13056760.creator: Ximena Ramos Salas, Brad Hussey, Angela S Alberga, Ted Kyle, Francine Small
pmc-13056760.description: BackgroundDespite decades of initiatives promoting individual behavior change, obesity rates remain high and continue to rise globally, indicating that what is commonly labelled as “obesity prevention” is not, in practice, preventing obesity. While health promotion strategies and policy interventions have demonstrated improvements in environments, health behaviors, and industry practices, their effects on obesity incidence and prevalence remain modest.

pmc-13124616.title: Cardiovascular risk in primary aldosteronism: inflammatory drivers, residual risk, and emerging combination strategies
pmc-13124616.creator: Haoze Liu, Zejun Wu, Xinzhe Liu, Yuyuan Hu, Kaixuan Zhang, Jiwen Shang
pmc-13124616.description: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is associated with a substantially higher cardiovascular risk than essential hypertension, a disparity that cannot be fully explained by blood pressure elevation alone. Clinical studies consistently demonstrate that cardiovascular morbidity and mortality often persist in patients with PA despite adequate blood pressure control and standard therapy, underscoring the existence of residual cardiovascular risk.

pmc-13189864.title: Choriocarcinoma Histologically Mimicking Epithelioid Trophoblastic Tumor – A Diagnostic Pitfall in Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia
pmc-13189864.creator: Ali Budi Harsono, Aisyah Shofiatun Nisa, Artha Falentin Putri Susilo, Rommy Andika Kurniawan, Gatot Nyarumenteng Adhipurnawan Winarno
pmc-13189864.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHistopathological diagnosis can be challenging because epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT) may closely mimic choriocarcinoma, particularly due to overlapping cytologic and architectural features of intermediate trophoblasts. Therefore, immunohistochemical studies are essential for accurate classification of GTN subtypes.Case IllustrationA 27-year-old woman, para 4 abortion 1, with a history of two curettage procedures for partial hydatidiform mole, presented with persistent post-curettage vaginal bleeding for five months and was admitted to the emergency department with severe anemia.

pmc-13570640.title: Rare Groin Hernias With Unusual Sac Contents: A Systematic Review of Anatomical Variants and Surgical Implications
pmc-13570640.creator: Christos-Pavlos Filippou, Dimosthenis Chrysikos, Theodore Troupis, Dimitrios Filippou
pmc-13570640.description: Groin hernias are commonly encountered in general surgical practice. Most of these hernias have a typical anatomical structure and contain the usual type of hernia sac content. Still, in some rare cases, a hernia may show abnormal anatomy or contain unexpected material within the sac, which can affect both how it presents clinically and the surgical approach needed for treatment.
